findings: first_retained_append_anchor recursively scans the actual finite R followed by [a]. The retained anchor guarantees a stopping point even when every element of R is omitted; no separate nonempty-retained-tail premise is assumed.

If the first scanned element is omitted, the recursive omitted block is extended by that element; if retained, the scan stops immediately. The result proves the exact split R++[a]=M++b::B, rejection of every M entry and retention of b.
filter_next_eq_of_first_retained filters that exact split. Rejection of M makes its filter empty, yielding R.filter p++[a]=b::B.filter p.

When the filtered tail is empty, comparing heads forces b=a and canonical List.next on [a] returns a. When the filtered tail starts at c, head equality gives c=b and next of the anchored filtered list is that head.

These first two lemmas do not need Nodup for their valid scan/anchored-next conclusions. The final firstCornerBlock theorem adds the actual parent Nodup and obtains its partition by invoking the scan, rather than requiring it as input.
The closed block a::(M++[b]) is proved a literal prefix of (a::R)++[a], with B as its exact suffix. Thus it follows the original closed anchored list consecutively, including the closing edge.
Rotating the Nodup parent by one proves Nodup of R++[a]. The exact split then gives M.Nodup. The anchor cannot lie in M because p a=true while every M entry is false.
Empty M, b=a, R=[], and a singleton retained filter all remain permitted. No unequal-endpoint or two-corner premise silently removes cases that later geometry must address.
The Boolean predicate and list remain generic in this packet. Actual owner/corner membership, actual corner-cycle next and geometric compression require the separate actual specialization.

The second proof uses an emptiness proposition and an existing nonempty-list cons witness, avoiding generalization of the list under the dependent List.next membership argument. It retains the original list, the same filtered-next statement and both empty/nonempty branches.
